newsitem.title: Australia: Australia race row MP forms "One Nation" party.
newsitem.headline: Australia race row MP forms "One Nation" party.

text.p: Australian politician Pauline Hanson, who created an international storm last year with her attacks on Asian immigration and Aboriginal welfare, is forming her own party and aims to become a major force in poltics.
"I'm really intending to have some say in the government," Hanson said, declaring an ambition to stand a candidate for every seat in the Australian parliament.
The party, as yet unlaunched, would be called "Pauline Hanson's One Nation", the Australian Electoral Commission announced in newspaper advertisements on Wednesday.
Hanson made headlines in Australia and beyond last September with her maiden speech in parliament which warned that the country was "in danger of being swamped by Asians".
Opinion polls showed that a majority of voters backed her anti-immigration views and the government of Prime Minister John Howard struggled to control the race debate she sparked.
Her criticisms that the mainstream Liberal and Labor parties were selling the country to foreigners also struck a chord.

"So closely associated are the Liberal and Labor party policies that really they're not addressing the real issues in this country, to do with the unemployment and the fact that our country is being sold off," she told reporters on Wednesday.
Hanson, an independent Queensland MP, has also criticised government policies giving special benefits to Aborigines on the grounds that they are the nation's most disadvantaged people.
Her choice of the name "One Nation" was greeted with derision.
"Well at least it wasn't Ein Reich," said Labor opposition Leader Kim Beazley. "So we have got to be grateful for small mercies."
Germany's World War Two dictator Adolf Hitler used the slogan Ein Volk, Ein Reich, Ein Fuehrer (one people, one nation, one leader) for his Nazi party.
"One Nation" was also a slogan that former Labor prime minister Paul Keating employed to describe a set of policies designed to bind Australia together.
